中东局势持续升温，国际油价周四大幅走高。


据央视新闻，据美国官员及其他知情人士的消息，美国和以色列军方已制定在美国中期选举结束后再次对伊朗发动军事打击的具体计划。据称，美以双方正在筹划一次时间较短但强度较高的军事行动，并加强联合演练，包括派遣军机飞越伊拉克，进行模拟打击训练。相关消息称，新一轮打击目标可能包括伊朗的能源基础设施、核设施，以及导弹和无人机武器库。部分美国官员认为，再次发动大规模军事行动可能进一步冲击伊朗经济，迫使伊朗在外交谈判中作出让步。


据《纽约时报》报道，与此同时，美国国务院下令非紧急政府雇员及其家属撤离沙特阿拉伯，理由是伊朗支持的胡塞武装对沙特平民目标的袭击持续升级。受上述消息提振，布伦特原油期货周四上涨1.71%，至每桶110.67美元；美国西得克萨斯中质原油（WTI）上涨1.42%，至每桶98.53美元。

分析人士指出，尽管油价上行压力明显，但当前能源价格对消费者的实际冲击或不及历史先例。Aptus Capital Advisors股票投资组合主管David Wagner表示，汽油支出目前仅占美国人可支配收入的约2.5%，远低于十年前约5%的水平，家庭抗压能力相对较强。

美以拟定具体打击方案，目标涵盖核设施与能源基础设施

据央视新闻援引美国官员及知情人士消息，美以军方正在推进一项"短暂但密集"作战行动的筹划，打击目标预计涵盖伊朗能源基础设施、核设施以及导弹与无人机库存。国防部长Pete Hegseth本周已赴以色列与总理内塔尼亚胡会面，就新一轮打击进行磋商；美以两国空军亦已加强演练，多次飞越伊拉克上空演练打击机动。


部分美国官员认为，一轮密集的三天军事行动足以对伊朗经济造成决定性打击，迫使其在核计划及霍尔木兹海峡控制权等问题上作出外交让步。然而，美国迄今在该方向已多次中途叫停：特朗普本月初在美以两军进入最高戒备状态、行动几乎箭在弦上之际，再度在最后关头叫停计划。


就目前进展而言，外交渠道依然开放，美方谈判人员正以"可能重返战争状态"作为筹码向伊朗施压。但据报道，伊朗谈判代表迄今拒绝在核计划问题上作出让步，坚持将该议题推迟至谈判后续阶段处理。

特朗普多次否决方案，计划落地存在重大不确定性

尽管军事筹备持续推进，此次打击能否最终实施仍存在诸多变数。特朗普今年已多次否决重返大规模军事行动的方案，包括本月初的那次。报道援引的官员称，美国军事资产——包括三艘航母、数千名海军陆战队员、战斗机及特种作战部队——要到11月初才能全部到位，而特朗普此前亦公开承诺在大选前不采取军事行动。


以色列定于10月27日举行的选举亦构成额外变数。分析人士指出，若内塔尼亚胡在选举中落败，其看守政府身份将使发动战争的政治可行性大为降低。以色列政治评论员Mazal Mualem表示：

"如果伊朗主动发动攻击，那是另一回事，但主动发起进攻性打击对他而言将极为困难。"

此外，报道指出，军事规划上的反复已在五角大楼内部造成"逐日摇摆"效应，令军事计划人员疲于应对。前五角大楼中东政策首席官员Dana Stroul亦表示，迄今为止的常规军事行动及严厉经济制裁均未能推动伊朗回到谈判桌，特朗普与内塔尼亚胡"都没有令人信服地阐明，更多战争将如何改变这一战略困境"。

伊朗扬言升级报复，矛头或指向沙特石油设施

面对新一轮打击威胁，伊朗方面已明确表示将扩大报复范围。伊朗官员称，一旦冲突重燃，其打击目标将从此前的商业船只和地区能源基础设施延伸至数据中心和海底互联网电缆，并强调此次战斗"既不会短暂，也不会有限"。


伊朗方面还明确将沙特能源基础设施列为潜在打击目标。德黑兰政治分析人士Peiman Salehi表示，若伊朗核设施遭到攻击，报复计划之一便是打击沙特主要炼油设施，包括沙特阿美，因为这将立即推高全球油价与能源价格。"这场战争让我们明白，向特朗普施压的最佳杠杆就是推高油价，因为这会伤害美国民众，"他说。


伊朗总谈判代表Gen. Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf的高级顾问Mahdi Mohammadi本周在社交媒体上表示，美方认为可以在72小时内结束又一轮对伊打击，是一种"幻想"，并称伊朗的反击将"更为猛烈、更具创造性、且与以往不同"。

items.title: 面对史上最强超级厄尔尼诺，全球市场或“无处可躲”！
items.summary:
超级厄尔尼诺正成为全球资产配置面临的一项系统性风险。农产品减产、能源价格波动与通胀压力可能相互叠加，并在高利率、高债务的宏观环境下进一步冲击新兴市场主权债、实物资产及碳信用项目。


Pictet资产管理公司投资组合经理Katie
items.text:
超级厄尔尼诺正成为全球资产配置面临的一项系统性风险。农产品减产、能源价格波动与通胀压力可能相互叠加，并在高利率、高债务的宏观环境下进一步冲击新兴市场主权债、实物资产及碳信用项目。


Pictet资产管理公司投资组合经理Katie Self表示，几乎可以确定，这将是有史以来最极端的厄尔尼诺事件，全球资产市场没有任何角落能够“完全免疫”。她将应对此轮气候扰动列为当前的“绝对优先”事项。


Man Group、T. Rowe Price等机构已相继发出预警或启动专项模型。据彭博此前报道，部分精品对冲基金也已围绕这一气候周期构建投资策略。与以往相比，本轮厄尔尼诺可能遭遇更高的利率、更沉重的债务负担和更频繁的市场抛售，使气候冲击更容易向多个资产类别传导。


宏观脆弱性放大冲击，利率与主权债成为前线


Anthropocene Fixed Income Institute分析师Kamesh Korangi和Rose Choy本周在研报中指出，当前宏观环境与历史上的厄尔尼诺周期存在显著差异。更高的利率、债务水平和市场波动，可能放大气候冲击对资产价格的影响。


两人点名印度尼西亚、巴西和哥伦比亚，认为这些国家的主权债市场较为脆弱，并警告风险可能向全球其他市场蔓延。厄尔尼诺对农业、能源和基础设施的冲击，可能加重发展中国家的财政压力，进而影响主权信用评级。


T. Rowe Price已针对规模达1650亿美元的新兴市场债券和股票投资组合建立定制化模型，以评估和管理相关风险。机构关注的已不只是农产品价格上涨，还包括气候冲击引发的通胀变化、利率调整及主权信用恶化。


能源市场也成为重要的交易方向。ZAMS Asset Management创始人兼首席投资官Zulfiqar Ali表示，冬季往往是气候、地缘政治与结构性因素交汇的关键时期，具备分析优势和风险管理能力的投资经理有望从中获得超额收益。


目前，围绕厄尔尼诺的策略涵盖通胀相关利率衍生品、能源商品方向性交易，以及可能受到干旱或洪涝影响的农业资产。据世界气象机构预测，此轮强厄尔尼诺大概率将持续至2027年初。


实物资产与碳信用项目面临直接冲击


对于持有土地、农业和林业资产的投资者，极端天气可能直接影响资产产出与估值。东南亚森林火灾、印度季风表现疲弱，以及南美部分地区洪旱并存，都已给相关资产带来压力。


法国巴黎银行资产管理公司自然资本策略负责人Jonathan Dean正密切监测印度尼西亚等地的森林火灾风险，评估火灾可能造成的碳信用项目损失。其管理策略规模超过5.6亿美元，资金来自国际金融公司等多家发展融资机构。目前，团队正与印尼当地项目开发商合作，借助保险工具和遥感技术评估风险、完善管理方案。


对于依赖森林保护、农业生产或碳信用收益的项目，极端天气不仅可能造成直接损失，还会增加未来现金流预测的不确定性。随着气候风险纳入资产定价，投资者也需要重新评估项目的收益稳定性及风险补偿是否充足。


气候适应技术成为新的配置方向


部分资管机构正将气候风险转化为投资机会。Pictet的Katie Self表示，其团队正寻找能够应对极端天气的技术企业，包括智能灌溉设备供应商、帮助作物在干旱条件下扎根更深的农业技术公司，以及城市防洪和雨水管理系统提供商。


Self管理的Pictet全球环境机遇基金规模达51亿美元。她指出，厄尔尼诺并非新现象，但如今发生在更高的全球气温基线上，气候变暖与极端天气叠加，可能显著加剧其影响。


从农业节水、作物抗旱到城市防洪，气候适应技术有望受益于相关需求增长。不过，需求扩大并不意味着相关资产必然上涨，技术商业化进度、项目回报和估值仍是投资决策的关键。


对全球资管机构而言，超级厄尔尼诺的真正挑战，在于气候冲击可能同时影响通胀、利率、主权信用和实物资产。在高债务、高利率的背景下，单一资产的风险对冲或许不足以应对跨市场传导，投资组合的整体抗压能力正面临考验。

两人点名印度尼西亚、巴西和哥伦比亚，认为这些国家的主权债市场较为脆弱，并警告风险可能向全球其他市场蔓延。厄尔尼诺对农业、能源和基础设施的冲击，可能加重发展中国家的财政压力，进而影响主权信用评级。
T. Rowe Price已针对规模达1650亿美元的新兴市场债券和股票投资组合建立定制化模型，以评估和管理相关风险。机构关注的已不只是农产品价格上涨，还包括气候冲击引发的通胀变化、利率调整及主权信用恶化。
能源市场也成为重要的交易方向。ZAMS Asset Management创始人兼首席投资官Zulfiqar Ali表示，冬季往往是气候、地缘政治与结构性因素交汇的关键时期，具备分析优势和风险管理能力的投资经理有望从中获得超额收益。
目前，围绕厄尔尼诺的策略涵盖通胀相关利率衍生品、能源商品方向性交易，以及可能受到干旱或洪涝影响的农业资产。据世界气象机构预测，此轮强厄尔尼诺大概率将持续至2027年初。
实物资产与碳信用项目面临直接冲击
对于持有土地、农业和林业资产的投资者，极端天气可能直接影响资产产出与估值。东南亚森林火灾、印度季风表现疲弱，以及南美部分地区洪旱并存，都已给相关资产带来压力。
法国巴黎银行资产管理公司自然资本策略负责人Jonathan Dean正密切监测印度尼西亚等地的森林火灾风险，评估火灾可能造成的碳信用项目损失。其管理策略规模超过5.6亿美元，资金来自国际金融公司等多家发展融资机构。目前，团队正与印尼当地项目开发商合作，借助保险工具和遥感技术评估风险、完善管理方案。
对于依赖森林保护、农业生产或碳信用收益的项目，极端天气不仅可能造成直接损失，还会增加未来现金流预测的不确定性。随着气候风险纳入资产定价，投资者也需要重新评估项目的收益稳定性及风险补偿是否充足。
气候适应技术成为新的配置方向
部分资管机构正将气候风险转化为投资机会。Pictet的Katie Self表示，其团队正寻找能够应对极端天气的技术企业，包括智能灌溉设备供应商、帮助作物在干旱条件下扎根更深的农业技术公司，以及城市防洪和雨水管理系统提供商。
Self管理的Pictet全球环境机遇基金规模达51亿美元。她指出，厄尔尼诺并非新现象，但如今发生在更高的全球气温基线上，气候变暖与极端天气叠加，可能显著加剧其影响。
从农业节水、作物抗旱到城市防洪，气候适应技术有望受益于相关需求增长。不过，需求扩大并不意味着相关资产必然上涨，技术商业化进度、项目回报和估值仍是投资决策的关键。
对全球资管机构而言，超级厄尔尼诺的真正挑战，在于气候冲击可能同时影响通胀、利率、主权信用和实物资产。在高债务、高利率的背景下，单一资产的风险对冲或许不足以应对跨市场传导，投资组合的整体抗压能力正面临考验。

items.title: 防范PHP高危漏洞，工信部等紧急发布提示！
items.summary:

此次漏洞波及范围极广，全球约七成网站底层依赖PHP运行，从政府服务到金融机构均面临直接安全威胁。网络安全公司Cloud
items.text:
工业和信息化部网络安全威胁和漏洞信息共享平台（NVDB）发布紧急提示，PHP存在两个远程代码执行超危漏洞，攻击者无需任何身份验证即可直接入侵目标系统，建议相关单位和用户立即排查并升级至最新安全版本。

此次漏洞波及范围极广，全球约七成网站底层依赖PHP运行，从政府服务到金融机构均面临直接安全威胁。网络安全公司Cloudflare披露，漏洞曝光后已检测到数百万次利用尝试；亚马逊则表示，黑客早在漏洞公开四天前便已着手尝试利用该缺陷。


在应对层面，芬兰、法国、荷兰等国率先将部分政府服务主动下线；日本多家航空、金融、消费品及游戏企业相继宣布服务中断；阿里云、腾讯云亦于事件曝光后发出紧急警告，要求客户尽快完成版本升级。

无需登录即可入侵，漏洞危害严重

此次被曝光的两个漏洞，核心风险在于攻击门槛极低。未经身份验证的攻击者可直接对运行PHP的服务器发动攻击，远程执行任意代码，进而导致服务器受控、敏感信息泄露及业务中断。


受影响的PHP版本范围广泛，包括：8.5系列低于8.5.12、8.4系列低于8.4.27、8.3系列低于8.3.36、8.2系列低于8.2.35，以及8.1系列及更早版本。


漏洞由美国两家网络安全机构Calif和Wiz的研究人员发现，借助OpenAI和谷歌的AI模型辅助分析后方才识别。值得关注的是，该漏洞此前已在系统中潜伏超过十年。


工信部在风险提示中明确列出应对优先级：相关单位和用户应立即开展全面排查，及时升级至PHP官方发布的最新安全版本。


对于短期内无法完成升级的机构，官方建议采取临时下线、关闭会话上传进度功能、网络隔离或访问限制等临时防护措施，同时加强网络安全监测，及时更换账号、口令和密钥等凭证。

多国选择主动下线，以时间换安全

PHP作为全球最广泛使用的服务器端脚本语言之一，为互联网基础设施提供底层支撑。网络安全公司Wiz估计，受影响的PHP语言驱动了全球约70%的网站，其中包括建站平台WordPress。


这一规模意味着，从个人博客、中小企业官网到政府公共服务平台，均潜在处于攻击者的打击范围之内。美国国家安全局（NSA）及欧洲网络安全机构相继就此发出警告，要求企业立即采取行动。


面对漏洞曝光后攻击尝试的急速攀升，多国政府和企业选择主动关停相关服务。


在欧洲，芬兰、法国、荷兰率先对部分政府服务采取预防性下线。澳大利亚信号局于周三深夜发布警告，敦促企业及用户尽快更新补丁，但仍有部分政府网站因此陷入无法访问状态。在亚太地区，韩国将私营部门网络危机预警级别上调，并召集国防部、科学与信息通信技术部及国家情报院官员举行紧急会议。


日本方面，航空公司全日空（ANA）宣布暂停网站及应用程序服务，包括Apple Wallet登机牌功能；野村证券旗下子公司及三菱UFJ金融集团（MUFG）暂停部分非核心服务，三菱UFJ表示停摆不影响支付业务；日本最大啤酒商朝日集团、铁路运营商京阪控股、游戏企业世嘉（Sega）和万代南梦宫（Bandai Namco）亦相继宣布对相关网站进行紧急维护或暂停部分功能。

中小企业和普通用户同样承压

尽管此次漏洞引发广泛关注，部分专业人士提示，不同类型机构面临的实际风险存在显著差异。


莫纳什大学学者Rashina Hoda表示，大型银行和企业通常不依赖PHP处理敏感交易，因此受到的直接冲击相对有限。然而，大量高度依赖WordPress等建站平台的中小型企业，其网站底层正是PHP，这类企业将面临更为迫切的修复压力。


Hoda同时警告，此次漏洞曝光可能引发网络诈骗和网络钓鱼攻击的激增。攻击者往往借助重大安全事件制造恐慌，诱导用户点击虚假"补丁链接"或提交账户信息。

items.title: 摩根大通：新云厂商融资承压难撼AI基建周期，科技板块今年仍有4000亿美元盈余
items.summary:
科技板块的内部造血能力，正在成为本轮AI资本支出周期最坚实的护城河。


近期市场对新云厂商（neocloud）融资模式可持续性的担忧升温，但摩根大通在最新的报告中表示，上述风险不足以动摇整体AI资本支出周期。关键理由在于：全球上市科技公司今年预计产生约2.2万亿美元经营性现金流，资本支出及研发支出合计约1.8万亿美元
items.text:
科技板块的内部造血能力，正在成为本轮AI资本支出周期最坚实的护城河。


近期市场对新云厂商（neocloud）融资模式可持续性的担忧升温，但摩根大通在最新的报告中表示，上述风险不足以动摇整体AI资本支出周期。关键理由在于：全球上市科技公司今年预计产生约2.2万亿美元经营性现金流，资本支出及研发支出合计约1.8万亿美元，两者相抵后科技板块整体仍有约4000亿美元的融资盈余——无需依赖外部融资即可维持当前投入规模。

报告同时指出，即便新云厂商的融资模式在最不利情景下陷入困境，其建设缺口完全可由超大规模云服务商（hyperscaler）等资产负债表更为稳健的科技企业填补。与此同时，摩根大通的整体股票仓位指标显示，市场持仓已从9月中旬的近期峰值明显回落，表明短期下行空间正在趋于收窄。

新云厂商体量有限，无力拖垮AI基建大盘

新云厂商——即专门向AI工作负载出租算力的专业化AI基础设施提供商——的融资隐忧过去一周持续发酵。问题的核心在于：其资本支出与收入之间存在时间错配，高收益债券市场的融资成本攀升正在压缩这一商业模式的运转空间。


然而从绝对体量来看，新云厂商在整个AI生态中的占比相当有限。


据摩根大通测算，在全球上市科技公司今年约2.2万亿美元的预计经营性现金流中，新云厂商仅贡献约300亿美元；在约1.8万亿美元的资本支出及研发支出中，新云厂商的对应规模约为800亿美元。摩根大通信贷研究团队指出，随着高收益债市场融资成本上升，公开上市的新云厂商可能需要调整融资结构，减少公司层面的债务融资，转而更多依赖股权融资及项目专项债务。


摩根大通股票研究团队亦指出，资金成本上升确实会压缩回报空间，但旺盛的算力需求也为厂商提供了向客户转嫁部分成本的可能性。即便最终证明这一逻辑未能成立，新云厂商的建设规模也可以由超大规模云服务商等拥有更雄厚资产负债表的科技企业来承接。

4000亿美元内部盈余构成AI周期安全垫

科技板块自给自足的融资能力，是摩根大通对AI资本支出周期保持信心的核心论据。


报告数据显示，今年科技板块的经营性现金流与资本支出之差约为4000亿美元的盈余。在摩根大通的压力情景测算中，即便科技板块此后五年（至2030年）每年将资本支出提升25%，同时现金流每年增长20%，到2030年仍将维持小幅盈余。这意味着，在相当长的时间窗口内，科技板块整体无需依赖外部资本市场输血即可支撑AI基建投入。


那么，科技公司为何仍在积极发债？


摩根大通解释称，科技板块在加大资本支出的同时，仍在维持大规模的股票回购计划，这才是外部融资需求的主要来源。一旦市场的融资压力从新云厂商蔓延至更广泛的科技公司，这些企业在原则上完全可以选择暂缓回购，并启动内部循环融资机制——即现金流盈余的芯片制造商等企业向存在资金缺口的新云厂商提供内部支持。


摩根大通此前的研究显示，AI资本支出与现金流周期的深层支撑，来自大型企业对AI的直接采购需求，据调查估计今年全球相关支出规模或可达1.5万亿美元。

半导体VaR冲击频率上升，仓位调整已现信号

摩根大通将近期AI基础设施股票的回调，置于半导体板块VaR冲击日趋频繁的结构性背景下加以解读。


自今年二季度起，即便AI周期基本面保持稳健，半导体VaR冲击也将变得更为频繁。原因在于，半导体（含存储芯片）在全球股票市场中的市值占比大幅攀升，其波动率相对大盘的溢价也随之走高。


从风险资本占用的角度测算，摩根大通估计，科技板块当前在MSCI ACWI指数中消耗的风险资本份额约为40%，远超其28%的市值权重；其中半导体行业占用的风险资本份额约为21%，同样高于其13%的市值权重——这意味着半导体相关公司实际上消耗了全球股票市场约五分之一的总风险资本。


这一特征已直接体现在对冲基金的行为上。


摩根大通数据显示，自9月下旬以来，半导体ETF（SMH US）的走势与HFRX股票对冲基金指数的日度表现高度同步，与今年4月初至7月末的情形如出一辙。在市场反弹阶段，这种联动反映了对冲基金对半导体的持仓集中度较高；而在回调阶段，则意味着风险限额触发后的被迫减仓会放大跌幅。


目前摩根大通的综合股票仓位指标显示，当前持仓已从9月中旬的近期峰值大幅下滑，包括CTA在内的趋势跟踪型投资者的半导体多头头寸似乎已基本消化。该行认为，上述仓位调整的推进，正在逐步收窄市场的短期下行空间。

items.title: 半年亏807亿美元、算力豪赌7500亿，Anthropic破产概率为何仅被定价17%
items.summary:
预测市场给出Anthropic17%的破产概率，折射出AI模型公司高资本开支模式下，市场对其生存能力的复杂判断。


据预测市场平台Polymarket最新数据，Anthropic在2028年底前宣告破产的概率仅为17%。这一定价与该公司本周曝光的IPO草案形成鲜明张力——招股草案显示，Anthropic
items.text:
预测市场给出Anthropic17%的破产概率，折射出AI模型公司高资本开支模式下，市场对其生存能力的复杂判断。


据预测市场平台Polymarket最新数据，Anthropic在2028年底前宣告破产的概率仅为17%。这一定价与该公司本周曝光的IPO草案形成鲜明张力——招股草案显示，Anthropic 2026年上半年净亏损超过807亿美元，算力基础设施承诺支出最高可达7500亿美元。

华尔街见闻文章此前写道，据《华尔街日报》援引Anthropic最新版S-1招股草案报道，807亿美元净亏损中约720亿美元为非现金会计调整项，实际运营亏损约87亿美元，但这一数字已超过2025年全年逾80亿美元的运营亏损总额。与此同时，公司2026年上半年营收达163亿美元，第三季度营收环比增长45%至168亿美元，显示出一定的商业化势头。


然而，营收增速的放缓已在潜在IPO买家中引发估值分歧。管理层在投资者日披露，营收环比增速从第一季度至第二季度的约140%大幅放缓至第三季度的45%至46%，促使部分机构投资者将参考估值区间从2万亿美元下调至约1.5万亿美元。Polymarket的17%破产概率定价，本质上是市场在押注：Anthropic的营收增长轨迹足以在资金耗尽之前实现规模化盈利——但这一赌注的前提条件正在变得愈发苛刻。


营收增长的隐忧：集中度风险与增速放缓


市场给予Anthropic较低破产概率的核心逻辑，在于其营收的快速增长。但这一增长本身存在结构性隐患。


招股书显示，2026年上半年163亿美元营收中，约20%即约32.6亿美元来自仅两家客户。 公司同时警告投资者，"在可预见的未来"，营收将持续高度集中于"有限数量的客户"，且许多大型企业客户并未签订长期合同，理论上可随时切换供应商。


与此同时，营收增速的放缓已引发机构投资者的重新定价。管理层在投资者日披露，环比增速从第一、二季度之间的约140%大幅放缓至第三季度的45%至46%。尽管45%的季度环比增速在绝对意义上仍属强劲，但与此前增速的落差，已足以促使部分机构将估值参考区间从2万亿美元下调至约1.5万亿美元。


Anthropic表示，2026年第二季度已实现经调整后的正利润，但在完整审计财务数据公布之前，"调整后"利润的具体口径仍有待厘清。


17%的定价逻辑：市场在押注什么


Polymarket 17%的破产概率定价，本质上反映了市场对以下核心判断的概率加权：Anthropic的营收增长轨迹能否在2028年底前覆盖其固定算力负债，同时维持足够的融资能力以弥补运营缺口。


支撑低破产概率的论据包括：营收增速仍处于高位；谷歌、亚马逊等战略投资者具有强烈的动机维持公司运营；IPO本身将提供新的资本补充渠道；以及807亿美元净亏损中的绝大部分为非现金项目，不构成即期现金压力。


但这一定价所隐含的风险在于，它可能低估了固定算力负债在营收增速持续放缓情景下的流动性压力，以及客户高度集中所带来的收入脆弱性。 AI模型公司高资本开支模式的可持续性，最终取决于一个尚未被历史数据充分验证的假设：算力投入能够以足够快的速度转化为可防御的、长期锁定的营收。


Anthropic的IPO，将是这一假设接受公开市场检验的第一次真正压力测试。


天文级亏损：807亿美元的两层结构


华尔街见闻文章写道，Anthropic的807亿美元半年净亏损，在会计层面由性质迥异的两部分构成。


其中约720亿美元为非现金会计调整项。随着公司私募估值在历次融资轮次中持续攀升，美国通用会计准则（GAAP）要求将向早期投资者发行的可转换票据及其他复杂融资工具的公允价值负债相应上调，由此在账面形成大规模"纸面亏损"。这一会计处理方式在高速融资的科技初创公司中并不罕见，但807亿美元的绝对规模仍属罕见。


剥离这一会计调整，公司上半年实际运营亏损仍高达约87亿美元，已超过2025年全年逾80亿美元的运营亏损总额。核心驱动因素在于算力支出的爆炸式增长：2026年上半年，Anthropic在计算资源与基础设施方面的直接支出接近90亿美元，较2025年上半年的23亿美元增长近四倍，甚至超过2025年全年73亿美元的算力总开支。


这意味着，在支付任何研究人员、管理层或销售人员薪酬之前，每一美元营收中已有逾55美分流向数据中心运营商与芯片供应商。这一成本结构，是理解Polymarket定价逻辑的关键起点。


7500亿算力账单：从弹性支出到不可撤销负债


Anthropic算力投入的真正风险，不在于规模本身，而在于其合同结构已从灵活的按需付费模式，演变为固定的、不可撤销的长期负债。


华尔街见闻文章提及，据《华尔街日报》报道，公司锁定的算力基础设施支出承诺已突破6000亿美元，若正在谈判的额外1500亿美元协议落地，总额将达到7500亿美元。根据最新招股草案，公司在未来七至十年内须承担约4500亿美元的云计算合同义务，且绝大多数协议明确注明"无论实际使用量如何均须支付"。


主要合同条款包括：与谷歌云签订1110亿美元合同；与亚马逊云服务（AWS）签订1100亿美元合同；与微软签订310亿美元合同；分别与AI云服务商Nscale和Lambda签订的合计最高860亿美元芯片租赁协议，租期延伸至2033至2034年。此外，公司还通过与博通的独立安排，承担了逾1600亿美元的谷歌TPU芯片租赁义务。


招股书还披露了一个供应侧困境：Anthropic已寻求超过AWS、谷歌与微软愿意提供的算力上限，部分原因在于三大超大规模云服务商日益将其视为直接竞争对手。 被迫转向替代供应商后，公司开始自建数据中心并与第三方设施运营商合作，而招股书坦承，这些运营商"运营历史有限"，可靠性存在不确定性。招股书同时提及，部分算力安排通过特殊目的载体（SPV）和私人信贷工具以表外形式融资，进一步增加了财务透明度方面的不确定性。

然而，营收增速的放缓已在潜在IPO买家中引发估值分歧。管理层在投资者日披露，营收环比增速从第一季度至第二季度的约140%大幅放缓至第三季度的45%至46%，促使部分机构投资者将参考估值区间从2万亿美元下调至约1.5万亿美元。Polymarket的17%破产概率定价，本质上是市场在押注：Anthropic的营收增长轨迹足以在资金耗尽之前实现规模化盈利——但这一赌注的前提条件正在变得愈发苛刻。
营收增长的隐忧：集中度风险与增速放缓
市场给予Anthropic较低破产概率的核心逻辑，在于其营收的快速增长。但这一增长本身存在结构性隐患。
招股书显示，2026年上半年163亿美元营收中，约20%即约32.6亿美元来自仅两家客户。 公司同时警告投资者，"在可预见的未来"，营收将持续高度集中于"有限数量的客户"，且许多大型企业客户并未签订长期合同，理论上可随时切换供应商。
与此同时，营收增速的放缓已引发机构投资者的重新定价。管理层在投资者日披露，环比增速从第一、二季度之间的约140%大幅放缓至第三季度的45%至46%。尽管45%的季度环比增速在绝对意义上仍属强劲，但与此前增速的落差，已足以促使部分机构将估值参考区间从2万亿美元下调至约1.5万亿美元。
Anthropic表示，2026年第二季度已实现经调整后的正利润，但在完整审计财务数据公布之前，"调整后"利润的具体口径仍有待厘清。
17%的定价逻辑：市场在押注什么
Polymarket 17%的破产概率定价，本质上反映了市场对以下核心判断的概率加权：Anthropic的营收增长轨迹能否在2028年底前覆盖其固定算力负债，同时维持足够的融资能力以弥补运营缺口。
支撑低破产概率的论据包括：营收增速仍处于高位；谷歌、亚马逊等战略投资者具有强烈的动机维持公司运营；IPO本身将提供新的资本补充渠道；以及807亿美元净亏损中的绝大部分为非现金项目，不构成即期现金压力。
但这一定价所隐含的风险在于，它可能低估了固定算力负债在营收增速持续放缓情景下的流动性压力，以及客户高度集中所带来的收入脆弱性。 AI模型公司高资本开支模式的可持续性，最终取决于一个尚未被历史数据充分验证的假设：算力投入能够以足够快的速度转化为可防御的、长期锁定的营收。
Anthropic的IPO，将是这一假设接受公开市场检验的第一次真正压力测试。
天文级亏损：807亿美元的两层结构
华尔街见闻文章写道，Anthropic的807亿美元半年净亏损，在会计层面由性质迥异的两部分构成。
其中约720亿美元为非现金会计调整项。随着公司私募估值在历次融资轮次中持续攀升，美国通用会计准则（GAAP）要求将向早期投资者发行的可转换票据及其他复杂融资工具的公允价值负债相应上调，由此在账面形成大规模"纸面亏损"。这一会计处理方式在高速融资的科技初创公司中并不罕见，但807亿美元的绝对规模仍属罕见。
剥离这一会计调整，公司上半年实际运营亏损仍高达约87亿美元，已超过2025年全年逾80亿美元的运营亏损总额。核心驱动因素在于算力支出的爆炸式增长：2026年上半年，Anthropic在计算资源与基础设施方面的直接支出接近90亿美元，较2025年上半年的23亿美元增长近四倍，甚至超过2025年全年73亿美元的算力总开支。
这意味着，在支付任何研究人员、管理层或销售人员薪酬之前，每一美元营收中已有逾55美分流向数据中心运营商与芯片供应商。这一成本结构，是理解Polymarket定价逻辑的关键起点。
7500亿算力账单：从弹性支出到不可撤销负债
Anthropic算力投入的真正风险，不在于规模本身，而在于其合同结构已从灵活的按需付费模式，演变为固定的、不可撤销的长期负债。
华尔街见闻文章提及，据《华尔街日报》报道，公司锁定的算力基础设施支出承诺已突破6000亿美元，若正在谈判的额外1500亿美元协议落地，总额将达到7500亿美元。根据最新招股草案，公司在未来七至十年内须承担约4500亿美元的云计算合同义务，且绝大多数协议明确注明"无论实际使用量如何均须支付"。
主要合同条款包括：与谷歌云签订1110亿美元合同；与亚马逊云服务（AWS）签订1100亿美元合同；与微软签订310亿美元合同；分别与AI云服务商Nscale和Lambda签订的合计最高860亿美元芯片租赁协议，租期延伸至2033至2034年。此外，公司还通过与博通的独立安排，承担了逾1600亿美元的谷歌TPU芯片租赁义务。

招股书还披露了一个供应侧困境：Anthropic已寻求超过AWS、谷歌与微软愿意提供的算力上限，部分原因在于三大超大规模云服务商日益将其视为直接竞争对手。 被迫转向替代供应商后，公司开始自建数据中心并与第三方设施运营商合作，而招股书坦承，这些运营商"运营历史有限"，可靠性存在不确定性。招股书同时提及，部分算力安排通过特殊目的载体（SPV）和私人信贷工具以表外形式融资，进一步增加了财务透明度方面的不确定性。
风险提示及免责条款
市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

items.title: Tokyo’s Four-Year Sushi Waitlist Is Now an Easier Reservation in NYC
items.summary:
A piece of sushi from Mitani. | Daniel Kruglikov

Currently, there’s a four-year waitlist to score one of the six seats at chef Yasuhiko Mitani’s Yotsuya sushi
items.text:
A piece of sushi from Mitani. | Daniel Kruglikov

Currently, there’s a four-year waitlist to score one of the six seats at chef Yasuhiko Mitani’s Yotsuya sushi counter, the famously inaccessible, introduction-only restaurant he opened in Tokyo 20 years ago. In New York, it’s considerably easier to eat Mitani’s sushi. All you need to do is hop on Tock and book seats for his newest Midtown restaurant — for a price.

In May, the chef quietly opened Mitani New York, his first U.S. restaurant, inside Midtown’s Lotte New York Palace hotel (455 Madison Avenue, at 50th Street). The seasonal dinner tasting menu costs $700, including tip, for roughly six appetizers and 10 to 12 pieces of sushi. The meal is built entirely around Japanese seafood sourced at fish-market auctions. At its core is what he calls “Mariage,” Mitani’s approach to pairing courses with wines, sake, and tea.

Serving wine with sushi is hardly new: High-end counters including the Upper East Side’s Sushi Noz and Midtown’s Jōji have incorporated serious French wines into their omakases for years. What distinguishes Mitani is the caliber of what’s poured by the glass — and how those drinks transform each course. At Mitani, the pairings include aged Champagne, Burgundy, and Sauternes, with bottles such as 2002 Cristal and 1981 Château d’Yquem opened for individual pours.

Mitani’s original restaurant in Japan holds a Tabelog Gold award. He opened it in 2006, followed by Kioicho Mitani Honten in 2016 and Kioicho Mitani Bettei in 2021. Regulars book Honten about a year ahead and Bettei about 10 months out.

Why diners can get a Mitani reservation in Manhattan

Mitani New York has two private dining rooms, each with a six-seat, L-shaped hinoki counter. Executive chef Kazuya Tsurta leads the cream-colored Oh Room. He spent five years at Kioicho Mitani and works alongside another Mitani alum, Daichi Shimamiya. Behind the counter, panels conceal a traditional Japanese refrigerator that cools using blocks of ice rather than electricity. The adjoining Koku Room counter is surrounded by charcoal-colored earthen walls. When Mitani is in New York, roughly three times a year, he works behind both counters.

There are two Mariage options. The entry-level one adds $800 to the $700 menu, bringing dinner to $1,500 per person; the premium version starts at $2,000 and can go higher based on the selections and diners’ requests. Yes, it’s an astonishing amount of money to spend on dinner — you could fly round-trip to Paris for less. The draw is experiencing how Mitani uses those wines to unlock flavors between food and drink, something he’d argue no other sushi counter in New York is doing at this caliber.

A Mariage meal might begin with kuruma ebi, briefly fried so its center remains raw beneath a tissue-paper-thin coating of batter, alongside 2002 Cristal. Fujinosuke salmon sashimi topped with Japanese black caviar might follow, alongside Juyondai Bessen Morohaku, a softly sweet junmai daiginjo sake. The sake’s sweetness offsets the salty caviar and rich fish.

Expect around six otsumami (small seasonal opening dishes), such as fried bafun uni beside a 1981 Château d’Yquem, part of the Premium Mariage. The uni’s salinity and the wine’s saffron-like sweetness make the course taste almost like a savory dessert. A later bite could include otoro, akami, and chutoro with Emmanuel Rouget Vosne-Romanée 1er Cru Cros Parantoux 2018 (that can run more than $1,400 a bottle).

The seafood Mitani selects in Japan travels from Haneda Airport to his New York counter in less than 24 hours. For each piece of nigiri, he adjusts the temperature of the fish and shari (seasoned rice), creating what he calls a “temperature gradient.” For example, Mitani serves otoro nigiri at 59 degrees and shari at 68 degrees.

A wine, sake, or gyokuro tea accompanies each opening dish, followed by another pour every few pieces of nigiri, amounting to roughly nine to 11 drinks across an 18-course menu.

Mitani says he began considering New York five years ago to create opportunities for his apprentices and to take on “the most challenging place in the world to do business.”

For now, Mitani offers something his Tokyo original doesn’t: a reservation you can make without an introduction or a multi-year wait.

items.title: Nyuzen Brown Ramen (入善ブラウンラーメン)
items.author: Ryo Iwa
items.summary: Mention ramen in Toyama, and Toyama Black is usually the first style that comes to mind. Yet Nyuzen, a small town in the prefecture’s east, once answered with
items.text:
Mention ramen in Toyama, and Toyama Black is usually the first style that comes to mind. Yet Nyuzen, a small town in the prefecture’s east, once answered with a different color. Nyuzen Brown Ramen (入善ブラウンラーメン) is a shrimp miso ramen that the local chamber of commerce youth group developed to promote the town.

Over time, it became a textbook example of Japan’s “B-grade gourmet” boom in the 2010s. This guide covers its origin, flavor, and ingredients, plus what we could confirm about its availability in September 2026.

What Is Nyuzen Brown Ramen?

Japanese speakers call this category B-kyū gurume, or B-grade gourmet. In general, the term means affordable local comfort food, often created or revived to put a town on the map. Nyuzen’s bowl fits that description closely, since its purpose was as much civic as culinary.


Quick Facts

Japanese name入善ブラウンラーメン (Nyūzen Buraun Rāmen)


HometownNyuzen Town, eastern Toyama Prefecture (Hokuriku region)


TypeB-grade gourmet ramen developed for town promotion


Developed byVolunteers from the Nyuzen Town Chamber of Commerce Youth Group


IntroducedAt the group’s 50th-anniversary event, November 2009


Original recipeNyuzen miso with shrimp extract, plus noodles made with deep ocean water


Restaurant guideline (2011)Use a miso seasoning blended with shrimp extract


ColorReddish brown


Availability (Sept 2026)Not confirmed at any restaurant; listed packaged products marked as discontinued


Can you still eat it today?


We could not confirm any restaurant currently serving Nyuzen Brown Ramen as of September 2026. This guide therefore treats it mainly as a local dish with a well-documented past. Check the restaurant section before planning a trip around it.


Where It Comes From

Nyuzen sits in the northeast corner of Toyama Prefecture, facing the Sea of Japan. Also, it spreads across the Kurobe River’s alluvial fan, where snowmelt from the Northern Alps resurfaces as spring water. The town also pumps deep ocean water from Toyama Bay.

According to Nyuzen Town, that water comes from a cold layer unique to the Sea of Japan and stays near 2°C all year. Meanwhile, several Japanese coastal towns have turned deep ocean water into a regional product, as Takahashi (2022) reviews. Nyuzen used it in the ramen’s noodles.

Why It Is Called “Brown Ramen”

The name also carries a playful local reference. A 2011 interview with the project’s leader, published on the regional site Kurobehan, says the team chose it with Toyama Black Ramen in mind. Toyama already had a famous black bowl, so Nyuzen went with brown.

The name reflects the broth’s actual appearance, too. Similarly, Nikkei described the soup in 2015 as slightly reddish brown. Later, Toyama Prefecture included the dish under brown in its “Toyama Color Food” program.

A Loose Guideline for Restaurants

Initially, you could only find the ramen as a souvenir pack or at local events. Soon, though, people kept asking where they could eat it in a restaurant. According to the 2011 interview, organizers then invited local shops to join. Their main condition was simple: use a miso seasoning blended with shrimp extract.

Everything else was left to each cook. As a result, by 2011 about 20 restaurants between Asahi Town and Namerikawa City reportedly offered a version. Some served it as tantanmen or jajamen, while one cooked it in a sizzling stone bowl. Whether that guideline still applies today is unclear.

What Does Nyuzen Brown Ramen Taste Like?

Official descriptions give the clearest picture. The maker, Zensho, describes a rich shrimp miso soup paired with deep-ocean-water noodles. Because restaurant recipes varied, the sweetness, saltiness, and shrimp intensity likely differed from shop to shop.

Broth and Aroma

Toyama’s official tourism site adds that the miso uses prefectural rice and soybeans, plus spring water from the Kurobe River fan. So the base is a miso broth, with shrimp as the distinguishing note. That shrimp aroma is likely to appeal most to diners who enjoy shellfish-based ramen.

Is it spicy? The 2011 interview described the original version as slightly spicy. However, don’t assume that holds for every restaurant version.

Noodles and Texture

Toyama’s tourism site describes the noodles as firm and springy, the texture Japanese speakers call shiko-shiko. That kind of noodle suits a heavy miso broth, since the soup clings to each strand. If you know Sapporo ramen, the basic miso-and-noodle pairing may feel familiar.

Toppings and Restaurant Twists

No official topping list exists. For example, Mynavi News reported in 2013 that one chain seared its chashu with miso and added shrimp powder. Meanwhile, a public bath in Asahi Town served a stone-grilled version, searing the noodles before adding soup.

Admittedly, that variation was part of the dish’s local appeal. Still, it makes the style difficult to define precisely.

What Is Nyuzen Brown Ramen Made From?

Zensho’s original recipe rests on three local components. Most descriptions still mention them together, even though restaurant versions were more flexible.


The original trio

Local miso

Made in Nyuzen from Toyama rice and soybeans, with spring water from the Kurobe River fan.


Shrimp extract

Blended into the miso. The 2011 restaurant guideline centered on this ingredient.


Deep ocean water

Worked into the noodles. Nikkei also mentions deep-sea salt in the soup.

Sources differ on one small detail. Zensho and Toyama’s tourism site place the deep ocean water in the noodles. However, Nikkei’s 2015 report mentions salt from the same water in the broth.

Stock and Dietary Requirements

Unfortunately, published sources do not identify the stock used by every restaurant. Diners avoiding meat, fish, or other animal-derived ingredients should ask each shop directly.

The historically documented recipe contains shrimp extract. Therefore, it does not suit vegetarians or vegans. Current ingredients may vary, so confirm them with the restaurant.

Allergens

Historical descriptions point to the ingredients below. Even so, they do not replace current allergen information from the restaurant or maker.


Shrimp: in the original miso seasoning, and sometimes as shrimp powder on top.

Wheat: in the noodles.

Soybeans: in the miso.


Anyone with a shellfish allergy should not order the dish without first confirming the ingredients and preparation with the restaurant. If the shop cannot confirm them, then skip it.

The History of Nyuzen Brown Ramen

A 50th-Anniversary Project

The story began with the youth group’s 50th anniversary in 2009. According to Kurobehan, members wanted a project that would still matter ten or twenty years later.

Notably, one member worked at Maruzen Shoyu, a local miso and soy sauce maker, according to Nikkei. He proposed miso ramen, partly because he loved ramen. Surprisingly, he told Kurobehan he had never eaten a miso ramen he truly enjoyed. The shrimp idea began almost as a whim, then went through rounds of testing.

From Event Stall to Souvenir Shelf

The group publicly introduced the ramen at its anniversary ceremony in November 2009. Guests asked for more, so the bowl soon appeared at local events such as the Nyuzen Ramen Festival. Because a volunteer group could not run a business, the organizers later established Zensho LLC in May 2010.

According to Zensho, its name joins 善 (zen) from Nyuzen with 商 (shō) from shōkōkai, the chamber of commerce. Its first product was a three-serving souvenir pack in a reusable miso-barrel tub. Later, that pack won the Governor’s Prize (知事賞) in the processed agricultural and marine products category. The contest was the Toyama Tourism Federation’s “Toyama Souvenir Best Selection 2011–2012” (富山のお土産ベストセレクション2011－2012).

Part of a Wider B-Grade Gourmet Boom

Nyuzen was not alone. Academic research, including Matsunaga (2013), has examined the broader use of B-grade gourmet foods in regional promotion across Japan. Nyuzen Brown Ramen fits neatly within that wider context.

In Toyama, the idea spread by color. Mynavi News reported in 2013 on a follow-up, Nyuzen Red Ramen, which kneads local chili into the noodles. Two years later, Nikkei pictured five colored Toyama bowls side by side: black, brown, red, green, and white.

Nyuzen Brown Ramen Today

The picture looks much quieter now. At the time of our September 2026 review, Zensho’s product page labeled the listed packaged products as discontinued. We could not verify whether any other packaged version remains available elsewhere.

The youth group’s own festival pages also show the same drift. In 2020, the group sold a Brown Ramen chashu bowl at the Nyuzen Ramen Festival. By contrast, the 2024 and 2025 vendor lists no longer include a Brown Ramen stall.

Nyuzen Brown Ramen vs Toyama Black Ramen

Since the brown bowl exists partly as a reply to the black one, a side-by-side look helps. The two share a prefecture, yet they differ in age, purpose, and flavor.

Nyuzen Brown RamenToyama Black Ramen

OriginNyuzen Town, eastern ToyamaToyama City, central Toyama

Born2009, as a town promotion projectPostwar years, as a meal for laborers

Seasoning baseMiso blended with shrimp extractDark soy sauce

ColorReddish brownNear black

FlavorSavory miso with shrimp aromaVery salty, with plenty of black pepper

DefinitionLoose 2011 guideline for restaurantsVaries by shop, but dark soy sauce is typical

Availability todayNot confirmed at restaurants (Sept 2026)Widely served across Toyama

Visit Toyama explains that Toyama Black began as a salty meal for postwar workers, first served in 1947 at the shop Daiki. By contrast, Nyuzen’s bowl grew out of a civic project six decades later. Read our Toyama Black Ramen guide for the full story.

Which One Should You Try?

In practice, Toyama Black is the one you can easily find today. It hits hard with salt and pepper, so locals often eat it with rice. Nyuzen Brown Ramen, meanwhile, is more of a local story worth knowing than a reliable stop on an itinerary.

Where to Eat Nyuzen Brown Ramen Today

Restaurant availability changes often, so this section separates documented history from what we could verify. In short, we could not confirm any restaurant serving the dish as of September 2026.

The Last Published Restaurant Map

Zensho’s restaurant map from around 2020 listed nine places. In September 2026, we checked each one against official websites and local organization pages.

Nyuzen Brown Ramen (入善ブラウンラーメン) is a shrimp miso ramen that the local chamber of commerce youth group developed to promote the town.

Over time, it became a textbook example of Japan’s “B-grade gourmet” boom in the 2010s. This guide covers its origin, flavor, and ingredients, plus what we could confirm about its availability in September 2026.
What Is Nyuzen Brown Ramen?

Japanese speakers call this category B-kyū gurume, or B-grade gourmet. In general, the term means affordable local comfort food, often created or revived to put a town on the map. Nyuzen’s bowl fits that description closely, since its purpose was as much civic as culinary.

Can you still eat it today?

We could not confirm any restaurant currently serving Nyuzen Brown Ramen as of September 2026. This guide therefore treats it mainly as a local dish with a well-documented past. Check the restaurant section before planning a trip around it.
Where It Comes From

Nyuzen sits in the northeast corner of Toyama Prefecture, facing the Sea of Japan. Also, it spreads across the Kurobe River’s alluvial fan, where snowmelt from the Northern Alps resurfaces as spring water. The town also pumps deep ocean water from Toyama Bay.

According to Nyuzen Town, that water comes from a cold layer unique to the Sea of Japan and stays near 2°C all year. Meanwhile, several Japanese coastal towns have turned deep ocean water into a regional product, as Takahashi (2022) reviews. Nyuzen used it in the ramen’s noodles.
Why It Is Called “Brown Ramen”

The name also carries a playful local reference. A 2011 interview with the project’s leader, published on the regional site Kurobehan, says the team chose it with Toyama Black Ramen in mind. Toyama already had a famous black bowl, so Nyuzen went with brown.

The name reflects the broth’s actual appearance, too. Similarly, Nikkei described the soup in 2015 as slightly reddish brown. Later, Toyama Prefecture included the dish under brown in its “Toyama Color Food” program.
A Loose Guideline for Restaurants

Initially, you could only find the ramen as a souvenir pack or at local events. Soon, though, people kept asking where they could eat it in a restaurant. According to the 2011 interview, organizers then invited local shops to join. Their main condition was simple: use a miso seasoning blended with shrimp extract.

Everything else was left to each cook. As a result, by 2011 about 20 restaurants between Asahi Town and Namerikawa City reportedly offered a version. Some served it as tantanmen or jajamen, while one cooked it in a sizzling stone bowl. Whether that guideline still applies today is unclear.
What Does Nyuzen Brown Ramen Taste Like?

Official descriptions give the clearest picture. The maker, Zensho, describes a rich shrimp miso soup paired with deep-ocean-water noodles. Because restaurant recipes varied, the sweetness, saltiness, and shrimp intensity likely differed from shop to shop.
Broth and Aroma

Toyama’s official tourism site adds that the miso uses prefectural rice and soybeans, plus spring water from the Kurobe River fan. So the base is a miso broth, with shrimp as the distinguishing note. That shrimp aroma is likely to appeal most to diners who enjoy shellfish-based ramen.
Is it spicy? The 2011 interview described the original version as slightly spicy. However, don’t assume that holds for every restaurant version.
Noodles and Texture

Toyama’s tourism site describes the noodles as firm and springy, the texture Japanese speakers call shiko-shiko. That kind of noodle suits a heavy miso broth, since the soup clings to each strand. If you know Sapporo ramen, the basic miso-and-noodle pairing may feel familiar.
Toppings and Restaurant Twists

No official topping list exists. For example, Mynavi News reported in 2013 that one chain seared its chashu with miso and added shrimp powder. Meanwhile, a public bath in Asahi Town served a stone-grilled version, searing the noodles before adding soup.
Admittedly, that variation was part of the dish’s local appeal. Still, it makes the style difficult to define precisely.
What Is Nyuzen Brown Ramen Made From?
Zensho’s original recipe rests on three local components. Most descriptions still mention them together, even though restaurant versions were more flexible.
The original trio
Local miso
Made in Nyuzen from Toyama rice and soybeans, with spring water from the Kurobe River fan.
Shrimp extract
Blended into the miso. The 2011 restaurant guideline centered on this ingredient.
Deep ocean water
Worked into the noodles. Nikkei also mentions deep-sea salt in the soup.
Sources differ on one small detail. Zensho and Toyama’s tourism site place the deep ocean water in the noodles. However, Nikkei’s 2015 report mentions salt from the same water in the broth.
Stock and Dietary Requirements
Unfortunately, published sources do not identify the stock used by every restaurant. Diners avoiding meat, fish, or other animal-derived ingredients should ask each shop directly.
The historically documented recipe contains shrimp extract. Therefore, it does not suit vegetarians or vegans. Current ingredients may vary, so confirm them with the restaurant.
Allergens
Historical descriptions point to the ingredients below. Even so, they do not replace current allergen information from the restaurant or maker.
Shrimp: in the original miso seasoning, and sometimes as shrimp powder on top.
Wheat: in the noodles.
Soybeans: in the miso.
Anyone with a shellfish allergy should not order the dish without first confirming the ingredients and preparation with the restaurant. If the shop cannot confirm them, then skip it.
The History of Nyuzen Brown Ramen
A 50th-Anniversary Project
The story began with the youth group’s 50th anniversary in 2009. According to Kurobehan, members wanted a project that would still matter ten or twenty years later.

Notably, one member worked at Maruzen Shoyu, a local miso and soy sauce maker, according to Nikkei. He proposed miso ramen, partly because he loved ramen. Surprisingly, he told Kurobehan he had never eaten a miso ramen he truly enjoyed. The shrimp idea began almost as a whim, then went through rounds of testing.
From Event Stall to Souvenir Shelf

The group publicly introduced the ramen at its anniversary ceremony in November 2009. Guests asked for more, so the bowl soon appeared at local events such as the Nyuzen Ramen Festival. Because a volunteer group could not run a business, the organizers later established Zensho LLC in May 2010.

According to Zensho, its name joins 善 (zen) from Nyuzen with 商 (shō) from shōkōkai, the chamber of commerce. Its first product was a three-serving souvenir pack in a reusable miso-barrel tub. Later, that pack won the Governor’s Prize (知事賞) in the processed agricultural and marine products category. The contest was the Toyama Tourism Federation’s “Toyama Souvenir Best Selection 2011–2012” (富山のお土産ベストセレクション2011－2012).
Part of a Wider B-Grade Gourmet Boom

Nyuzen was not alone. Academic research, including Matsunaga (2013), has examined the broader use of B-grade gourmet foods in regional promotion across Japan. Nyuzen Brown Ramen fits neatly within that wider context.

In Toyama, the idea spread by color. Mynavi News reported in 2013 on a follow-up, Nyuzen Red Ramen, which kneads local chili into the noodles. Two years later, Nikkei pictured five colored Toyama bowls side by side: black, brown, red, green, and white.
Nyuzen Brown Ramen Today

The picture looks much quieter now. At the time of our September 2026 review, Zensho’s product page labeled the listed packaged products as discontinued. We could not verify whether any other packaged version remains available elsewhere.

The youth group’s own festival pages also show the same drift. In 2020, the group sold a Brown Ramen chashu bowl at the Nyuzen Ramen Festival. By contrast, the 2024 and 2025 vendor lists no longer include a Brown Ramen stall.
Nyuzen Brown Ramen vs Toyama Black Ramen
Since the brown bowl exists partly as a reply to the black one, a side-by-side look helps. The two share a prefecture, yet they differ in age, purpose, and flavor.

In practice, Toyama Black is the one you can easily find today. It hits hard with salt and pepper, so locals often eat it with rice. Nyuzen Brown Ramen, meanwhile, is more of a local story worth knowing than a reliable stop on an itinerary.

items.title: New York, New York—Why We All Want To Be A Part of It
items.author: Gary Shteyngart
items.summary: As an almost lifelong citizen of New York City in his mid-50s, I go through the usual phases of “What have they done to my beloved city?” and “Hmm, things
items.text:
As an almost lifelong citizen of New York City in his mid-50s, I go through the usual phases of “What have they done to my beloved city?” and “Hmm, things aren't as bad as I thought they were.” Right now I'm definitely in the second stage of my relationship with Gotham. What's changed? The answer nearly everyone gives is “da Knicks.” I'm not a huge sports fan, but when it felt like the whole city was dancing around me and Spike Lee was throwing block parties in Fort Greene, it was hard not to get caught up in the joy. And then, to up the good-vibes ante, the World Cup came our way, and Norwegian soccer fans were Viking-rowing in Times Square.

The other thing that changed was the answer to the perennial question that haunts this super-expensive city: Who is New York for? The election of Zohran Mamdani as mayor was not welcomed by everyone (though a 58 percent approval rating in a city as contentious as New York is not bad at all), but it seemed to signal that the cost-of-living issue—the main plank on which Mamdani ran—had come to a head. Why does this matter? Because New York is only as great as its citizens, and that means continuing its legendary diversity—not just racial and ethnic but also economic diversity. It is a beacon for immigrants from around the world, but it is also a home for people who aren't centimillionaires: the teachers, the social workers, and those in the service industry who are essential to every visitor's impression of the city.

What this means to me on a day-by-day level is that, because of this economic and cultural diversity, New York is still the best walking city in America and perhaps the world. The Italians have their evening passeggiata, and Spaniards practice the splendid art of the tapear, hopping from tapas joint to tapas joint in search of satisfaction and tipsiness. I head out on great all-around-the-world culinary feasts, which can be found in nearly every corner of New York.

I'll start in Queens, in the Jackson Heights–Elmhurst-Woodside axis. I appreciate Mayor Mamdani's love of Kebab King, but my favorite Pakistani joint is Dera, whose nehari is the best beef stew in the world (go ahead, Mayor, fight me on this). Then I head over to Michelada House II for that eponymous jet fuel and the spicy hubcap-size crusty bread roll known as the torta de chilaquiles, then saunter down Roosevelt Avenue to the Himalayan Yak for some adorable momos before finishing up at the tiny 969 NYC Coffee, which, in addition to resurrection-level espressos, sells fresh salmon onigiri and other toothsome Japanese snacks (yes, they have matcha—I knew you'd ask). Total cost for three hours of intense pleasure? I don't know, maybe 40 bucks? Of course, I have a Manhattan version of this trek, starting with the odd dive bar that also happens to serve excellent Malaysian food (it's called Fish Market and it's in, of all places, the Seaport) and ending perched on a barstool at the Viet-Franco-who-knows-what masterpiece that is Ha's Snack Bar on the Lower East Side.

New York will always be up and down and all around. The rich will covet it, the poor will hang on, and, hopefully, the middle class will continue to grow. And in another 50 years, when this waterfront city may very well be laced by canals and have wind turbines lean precariously off its skyscrapers, it will still be my home—and for those who visit, a place of endless welcome.

This article appeared in the November 2026 issue of Condé Nast Traveler. Subscribe to the magazine here.
